# Microsoft Azure Event Grid management client library for .NET

Microsoft Azure Event Grid is a highly scalable, serverless event broker that you can use to integrate applications using events. Events are delivered by Event Grid to subscriber destinations such as applications, Azure services, or any endpoint to which Event Grid has network access. The source of those events can be other applications, SaaS services and Azure services.

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Event Grid resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Event Grid management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.EventGrid
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

proposals.explanation: Supplies sync and async GetAll returning NetworkSecurityPerimeterConfigurationData pageables by constructing the corresponding collection-result types with domain scope, parsed subscription GUID, resource-group/name and a cancellation-bearing RequestContext.

proposals.subtype: Explicit data-model enumeration delegates to list operations
proposals.explanation: Declares generic sync/async enumerable interfaces for perimeter data and explicitly implements their enumerators plus nongeneric IEnumerable by delegating to GetAll/GetAllAsync, propagating async cancellation.

proposals.explanation: Supplies CreateResourceIdentifier with separate perimeterGuid and associationName arguments, interpolating their dot-joined value into the domain networkSecurityPerimeterConfigurations resource path and constructing ResourceIdentifier.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The path-building overload is explicitly implemented in the Customized resource partial.

proposals.explanation: Adds cancellation-only Get/GetAsync that call SplitAssociationName(Id), build and process scoped REST requests, parse perimeter data, throw RequestFailedException for a null parsed value and wrap non-null data in DomainNetworkSecurityPerimeterConfigurationResource while preserving the raw response.

proposals.explanation: Implements sync/async Reconcile by splitting the identifier through the helper, sending a scoped request, constructing a data operation with AzureAsyncOperation finalization, optionally waiting for Completed, and returning a compatibility operation supplied with a data-to-domain-resource conversion lambda.

proposals.explanation: Adds DEBUG-conditional ValidateResourceId comparing the collection-parent identifier's resource type with EventGridDomainResource.ResourceType and throwing ArgumentException on mismatch.

proposals.explanation: Adds sync/async Exists validating the name and sending a scoped Get request directly through Pipeline.Send; status 200 returns true, 404 returns false and every other status throws RequestFailedException, preserving the raw response and recording exceptions in a diagnostic scope.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit request dispatch and status-switch behavior are supplied in the Customized collection rather than Generated source.

proposals.handwrittenRationale: The nullable-response status switches and typed conversion calls are explicit bodies in the Customized collection.

decisions.reason: The Customized partial actively suppresses the named enum-parameter factory and implements a string-parameter factory constructing UnknownStaticRoutingEnrichment. The cited lines support the model-factory replacement; the comment's claim about a generated compiler error is not independently verified.

The suppression names EventGridInputSchemaMapping with InputSchemaMappingType and the Customized partial implements the corresponding string-taking UnknownInputSchemaMapping factory. Generator production of such a factory is plausible, not demonstrated.

The suppression targets the EndpointType signature and the cited implementation accepts a string, converts or defaults the discriminator, and constructs UnknownEventSubscriptionDestination in a Customized source file.

The active DeliveryAttributeMapping suppression and the replacement string-discriminator factory are both shown; the implementation passes the supplied name and converted or default discriminator to UnknownDeliveryAttributeMapping.
The active enum-parameter suppression and handwritten AdvancedFilter(string, string) factory show a distinct public model-factory replacement that constructs UnknownAdvancedFilter.
The suppression names the DeadLetterEndPointType signature; the Customized factory replaces it with a string-taking UnknownDeadLetterDestination constructor call, including null-to-default handling.
The cited active suppression and EventGridFilter(string, string) implementation show a handwritten string-discriminator factory constructing UnknownFilter with the supplied key.

The factory is handwritten and valid, but its distinctive reusable behavior is copying or defaulting collection inputs rather than merely being a model factory. Use the existing defensive-copy pattern; the constructor body supports no claim about unseen generated constructor behavior.

finding.subtype: Private-link model factory copies or defaults list inputs
finding.explanation: The public EventGridPrivateLinkResourceData factory forwards resource and group metadata while constructing fresh lists from requiredMembers and requiredZoneNames, using empty lists when either input is null.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The factory's new-list construction is explicit in the Customized factory partial outside src/Generated.

decisions.reason: The Customized collection explicitly supplies both data-valued GetAll methods and wires generated collection-result helpers with domain scope and request context. The generated pager helpers are not themselves counted.

The interface declaration and three explicit enumerators are handwritten in Customized and add enumerable API shape, distinct from the GetAll methods; async cancellation is forwarded to the pageable and enumerator.

Three active CodeGenSuppress attributes in the Customized partial target the indicated identifier and Get signatures, a separate API-surface-shaping behavior. The actual generated declarations and whether suppression removed them are not present, as the proposal explicitly acknowledges.

The cited handwritten overload constructs a resource identifier from five strings and joins perimeterGuid and associationName with a dot; the reusable identifier-construction pattern is plausible for generator support.

Both Customized bound Get methods split Id, create scoped REST requests, parse the data response, reject a null model and construct a typed resource. The cited implementation supports these behaviors without depending on the unprovided SplitAssociationName body.

The handwritten Reconcile pair makes a scoped request, constructs an operation with the stated final-state mode, optionally waits, and returns a custom operation with a typed-resource projection. This is a wrapper/result-shaping customization, not a finding about the generated poller itself; the wrapper internals are unavailable.

Customized GetAll methods wrap data pageables with lambdas constructing domain resource objects, and the private methods provide scoped collection-result inputs. This is handwritten item projection; generated paging internals are not counted.
The Customized collection declares resource-valued enumerable interfaces and explicitly forwards all three enumerators to GetAll/GetAllAsync, adding API shape distinct from item projection.

The code constructs an ArmResource wrapper and exposes HasData/Data, not a largely handwritten client; the original Hand-written client category and client-over-generated pattern misclassify it. The typed resource wrapper is explicitly handwritten, though its interactions with unseen partials are unverified.

finding.subtype: Typed ARM resource wrapper tracks data availability
finding.explanation: The domain private-link ArmResource supplies protected and internal constructors; its data constructor stores the model and marks HasData, while Data returns that model only when present and otherwise throws InvalidOperationException.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The typed resource constructors and HasData/Data members are implemented in a Customized source file outside src/Generated.

decisions.reason: The static factory in Customized assembles the domain private-link ARM resource path from four arguments and constructs ResourceIdentifier; this is distinct from the wrapper's data-availability behavior.

The cited type check is a DEBUG-conditional identifier argument guard, not retry logic or response error handling. Other is the guideline category for this local argument-validation behavior; Conditional means constructor calls may be omitted in non-DEBUG builds.

finding.explanation: ValidateResourceId checks that the identifier's resource type matches the domain private-link resource type and throws ArgumentException when it does not; the call from the constructor is conditional on DEBUG.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The static expected type, constructor call, Conditional attribute and comparison body appear in Customized rather than src/Generated.

decisions.reason: Get and GetAsync on the Customized typed resource construct a resource-group facade, use the stored Id's names and forward to its scoped Get, then invoke compatibility conversion. The conversion helpers' internal behavior is not supplied.

The resource explicitly implements both model-serialization interfaces and delegates Create/format to a new data model and Write to Data. It does not handwrite a property-by-property JSON codec; the pattern describes forwarding rather than codec replacement.

These are ArmCollection constructors wiring diagnostics, a REST client and an API-version fallback, not a largely handwritten client replacing a generated client. Other captures collection initialization without attributing behavior to unseen generated internals.

finding.subtype: Typed resource collection initializes a version-selected REST client
finding.explanation: The internal collection constructor retrieves a resource API version, initializes diagnostics, and constructs a private-link REST client with that version or the literal 2025-07-15-preview fallback.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The constructor and REST client initialization are explicit in a Customized ArmCollection source file outside src/Generated.

decisions.reason: This checks a collection parent's ResourceType under a DEBUG-conditional call; it is local argument validation rather than retry/error-response behavior. No release-build validation should be inferred.

finding.explanation: ValidateResourceId compares the collection identifier's resource type to the domain resource type and throws ArgumentException on mismatch; its constructor invocation is conditional on DEBUG.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The Customized ArmCollection constructor, Conditional attribute and validation implementation show this handwritten guard outside src/Generated.

decisions.reason: Both typed Get overloads validate the name and call the mockable resource-group facade with the parent/domain/name arguments, then adapt the response through compatibility helpers. Their internal conversion semantics are outside the captures.

The Customized GetAll pair instantiates scoped collection results and pageable wrappers with explicit internal-model-to-domain-resource conversion lambdas; the generated collection result alone is not being counted.
Both handwritten Exists methods send the scoped Get and explicitly map 200 to true, 404 to false, and all other statuses to RequestFailedException while preserving the response.

GetIfExists and its async counterpart have separate status switches yielding a typed resource for 200, NoValueResponse for 404 and RequestFailedException otherwise, which is distinct from boolean Exists behavior.

The Customized collection explicitly declares the generic enumerable interfaces and implements generic, nongeneric and async enumerators by forwarding to its public list methods. This API-shape behavior is distinct from constructing/projecting the pageables.

limitations: Only seven of 922 eligible source files (1023 discovered files) were captured; 34 named customization files were excluded. These observations cannot establish library-wide absence.

The generated factories, enum definitions, historical GA/main APIs and compiler output are absent. Comments about internal discriminators, malformed global names and CS1001 are not independently established facts; the suppressions prove requested signatures, not actual generated-member removal.

SplitAssociationName, operation adapters/sources, compatibility conversion helpers, pageable wrappers and collection-result internals are absent. Calls and supplied conversion lambdas are observed, not their complete splitting, response-preservation, continuation or polling algorithms.
Reconcile uses AzureAsyncOperation finalization and optional waits but does not supply the underlying poller implementation in this request.
Resource and collection type guards are DEBUG-conditional, not unconditional release-build validation. Route-building interpolation does not show separate validation or escaping of every argument.

The collection's direct REST client has a null-only version fallback; facade-based Get operations use a different delegated route, so the constructor does not prove one fixed version across all calls.

Readme/service descriptions and compatibility comments do not establish service-caused generator gaps. Generator addressability is a plausible reusable opportunity, not proof of existing capabilities or measured reductions.

Coverage is partial: seven captured source files out of 922 eligible files and 34 listed skipped Customized files; omitted files may contain additional customizations. No package-wide absence conclusion is possible.

The captures omit generated declarations, other partials and compatibility-helper implementations, so the resulting public surface, actual suppression effects, conversion internals and runtime behavior cannot be independently established from this request.

Comments describing GA compatibility, generator failures and service history are unverified context, not independent proof of those causes. Generator-addressable yes denotes a plausible generalizable feature, not proof of an existing generator capability.
